news.summary: US equities rose in the shortened Friday session. The S&P 500 added 1.60% to finish a week in which it gained 5.6%. The Nasdaq Composite led the three major indexes on Friday even as Treasury yields rose.
news.coverage: The cash market closed at 13:00 New York time on Friday, 02:00 Saturday in Singapore. All quoted levels are closing observations. The weekly S&P figure is from AP’s closing report.
happened: The S&P 500 closed at 7,297.49, up 114.71 points from Wednesday. The Nasdaq Composite gained 543.70 points, or 2.31%, to 24,129.50.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 591.99 points, or 1.18%, to 50,774.94. All three comparisons use Wednesday’s close because the exchanges observed Thanksgiving on Thursday.
The 10-year Treasury par yield reached 4.94%, up from 4.85% on Wednesday. Equities and benchmark yields both ended the holiday week higher than at Wednesday’s close.
key_points: The Nasdaq outpaced the Dow by about 1.13 percentage points on Friday. These index moves show how differently the two benchmarks participated in the rebound.
The S&P 500’s 5.6% weekly rise includes the earlier sessions. Friday alone accounted for a 1.60% gain.
watch: At the next full US session, compare the Nasdaq and Dow with these closing levels to see whether the rally broadens.

bonds.summary: Treasury yields rose across the two- to thirty-year maturities after Thanksgiving. The 10-year rose nine basis points to 4.94%. The latest verified corporate spreads cover an earlier observation date.
bonds.coverage: Treasury figures come from the dated official XML curve. The ICE figures come from FRED’s 11:46 US Central time refresh on Friday. A 27 November corporate spread observation was unavailable at cutoff.
happened: The two-year Treasury par yield reached 4.69%, up eight basis points from Wednesday. The five-year reached 4.74%, up nine basis points.
The 10-year rose from 4.85% to 4.94%, and the 30-year rose from 5.24% to 5.33%. The 10-year premium over the two-year edged up from 24 to 25 basis points.
In its 27 November update, FRED showed ICE investment-grade and high-yield option-adjusted spreads of 99 bp and 377 bp for both 25 and 26 November. On 24 November they were 98 bp and 372 bp.
key_points: The larger recent widening was in high yield, at five basis points from Tuesday to Wednesday, versus one basis point for investment grade. The holiday-dated rows repeated Wednesday’s levels.
Treasury par yields measure the benchmark rate at specific maturities. Corporate option-adjusted spreads measure the extra yield over a benchmark and have a different reporting lag.
watch: Check the first published 27 November corporate observations before attributing a widening or tightening in spreads to Friday’s equity rebound.
Track whether the 10-year sustains its rise alongside the two-year at the next Treasury observation.

earnings.summary: Mountain Province Diamonds sold more than twice as many carats as a year earlier, yet its quarterly net loss widened to C$371.7m. The fall in its realised diamond price and the subsequent transfer of its mine interest are central to reading the result.
earnings.coverage: The Canadian issuer released its September-quarter figures at 16:30 EST on Friday, 05:30 Saturday in Singapore. Coverage is limited to this verified result. Amounts are Canadian dollars.
happened: For the quarter ended 30 September, sales rose to C$49.8m from C$29.2m. The company sold 913,255 carats against 409,081 a year earlier, while its average realised price fell to C$55 from C$71 per carat.
The loss from mine operations widened to C$38.4m from C$3.7m. The net loss was C$371.7m, against C$55.9m a year earlier, and included a derecognition and impairment charge.

After quarter-end, De Beers obtained the company’s 49% interest in Gahcho Kué and released Mountain Province from the corresponding joint-venture obligations. Specified lenders agreed to a six-month payment standstill.
key_points: Revenue grew because the company sold more carats despite the lower price per carat. The mine operating loss and the larger net loss measure different costs.
The September-quarter mine sales predate the transfer. Using those sales as a run rate would assume ownership the company has since relinquished.
watch: Look for terms on the remaining debt before the standstill expires. The option to repurchase the mine interest before 31 December 2029 depends on funding and diamond-market conditions.

economy.summary: US shoppers spent $9.7bn online by early Friday evening, up 12.8% from the comparable period last year. Separately, the Federal Reserve released weekly data on bank credit and reserve balances.
economy.coverage: Adobe’s 18:30 EST reading corresponds to 07:30 SGT. Reuters published the update at 08:06 SGT. The Fed scheduled H.8 and H.4.1 for 05:15 and 05:30 SGT respectively. The US retail day was still in progress at cutoff.
happened: Adobe Analytics tracked $9.7bn of US online purchases by 18:30 EST on Black Friday. Reuters reported Adobe’s full-day forecast range of $13.0bn to $13.4bn.
For the week to 25 November, reserve balances at the Fed averaged $2.964tn, down $16.0bn from the preceding weekly average. The single Wednesday observation was $2.929tn.
Seasonally adjusted commercial bank credit rose from $20,134.7bn to $20,147.4bn between 11 and 18 November. Loans and leases increased by $1.8bn over that week.
key_points: The spending figure covers online transactions through a specified hour. It gives an early read on sales dollars, with in-store purchases and retailer margins outside its scope.
The two Fed releases describe different weeks. The bank-credit observation is dated 18 November and the reserves observation is dated 25 November.
watch: Compare Adobe’s final total with the $13.0bn–$13.4bn forecast when full-day data arrive.
In the next weekly releases, check whether loans take a larger share of bank-credit growth and whether the reserve decline persists.

news.summary: The US goods deficit widened sharply as imports outpaced exports. EU leaders nominated Pablo Hernández de Cos to head the ECB. In Norway, the operating subsidiary of Norse Atlantic resolved to file for bankruptcy.
news.coverage: Full Singapore day, reconstructed with releases through 23:59 SGT. Norse announced the petition decision at 21:00 SGT and Census published at 21:30 SGT. Friday’s New York stock close fell in Saturday’s edition.
happened: The US Census Bureau’s advance report put the October goods deficit at $149.5bn, up from $135.1bn in September. Imports rose $21.1bn over the month and exports rose $6.7bn.

The European Council proposed Hernández de Cos to succeed Christine Lagarde, who is due to leave on 7 February 2027. Leaders also proposed Laurence Boone and Markus Brunnermeier for the ECB’s executive board.

Norse Atlantic said its Norwegian operator would petition the Agder District Court. Flights were cancelled and ticket sales stopped. The listed parent and its UK subsidiary were pursuing a solution for their remaining business.

Imperial’s board said it had received no approach and had held no talks about Altria’s possible bid. Altria had already disclosed that it was considering a cash offer and discussing a possible disposal of part of the business with a third party.
key_points: The European Council still has to consult the European Parliament and the ECB Governing Council before a formal appointment. The presidency carries an eight-year term.
Altria has yet to announce a firm bid or a price. Imperial’s response adds the target board’s account of contacts.
watch: Watch for the two consultations and the European Council’s formal decision.
Altria faces a 17:00 London deadline on 24 December to declare its intentions, unless the UK Takeover Panel grants an extension.

bonds.summary: Norse Atlantic’s Norwegian operating company decided to file for bankruptcy after failing to secure a path to continued operations. Earlier, Kiwibank priced NZ$200m of subordinated notes with a 5.17% initial coupon.
bonds.coverage: The recap includes Kiwibank’s final terms at 07:40 SGT and Norse’s announcement at 21:00 SGT. Friday’s US Treasury close and the FRED spread refresh both fell after Singapore midnight.
happened: The board of Norse Atlantic Airways AS resolved to file a bankruptcy petition. The group said the court would appoint a trustee. The announcement concerned the Norwegian operating subsidiary.
Kiwibank allocated the full NZ$200m at a margin of 120 basis points over the swap rate. The issuer reported about 1.7 times coverage at that margin, excluding lead managers’ trading interest.
Interest is fixed at 5.17% per year until 4 June 2032. If the notes remain outstanding, the coupon resets quarterly to the three-month bank bill rate plus 120 basis points.
The final terms set maturity for 4 June 2037. Kiwibank expects issuance on 4 December 2026 and NZX quotation under KWB3T2 on 7 December.
key_points: The Norwegian operator, listed parent and UK subsidiary are separate legal entities. The petition decision alone does not establish a recovery rate for claims against any of them.
The 5.17% figure is the initial contractual coupon. Secondary-market yields will depend on traded prices.
A holder could remain invested beyond June 2032 because redemption at the first call date is optional.
watch: Follow the court process and separate statements on the parent and UK business before assessing creditor recoveries.
Check settlement on 4 December and the first eligible traded price after quotation.

earnings.summary: Meituan returned to a quarterly profit as core local commerce recovered. In New Zealand, disposals at Green Cross Health and Burger Fuel affected otherwise comparable half-year results.
earnings.coverage: Full-day recap using Meituan’s 27 November Hong Kong filing for the three months to September and the two NZX releases for the six months to September. Meituan reports in renminbi. Both New Zealand companies report in NZ dollars.
happened: Meituan’s third-quarter revenue rose 21.6% year on year to RMB115.56bn. It earned RMB2.07bn after a loss of RMB18.63bn a year earlier. Operating profit reached RMB2.74bn after a RMB19.76bn operating loss.
Green Cross Health reported NZ$196.7m in profit attributable to shareholders, including a NZ$188.1m gain on its medical division sale, completed on 31 July.

In its continuing pharmacy business, revenue rose 9% to NZ$197.7m and operating profit rose 3% to NZ$7.0m. The company cited pressure on margins from a shift toward high-value, lower-margin medicines.
Burger Fuel reported NZ$948,749 in profit after tax, up 11.7%. Operating revenue excluding IFRS 16 interest income fell 3.9% to NZ$11.8m after the Ponsonby store passed to a franchisee.
key_points: At Meituan, core local commerce moved from a RMB14.07bn operating loss to a RMB5.70bn operating profit. New initiatives still recorded a RMB1.31bn operating loss.
Green Cross’s pharmacy operating profit offers a baseline for assessing the continuing business after the disposal.
Burger Fuel said operating revenue would have grown excluding the ownership change. It ended September debt-free with NZ$5.26m cash.
watch: Track whether Meituan’s core commerce profit can cover new-initiative losses as well as unallocated costs.
Track pharmacy operating profit alongside sales in Green Cross’s first full half following the sale.
Compare Burger Fuel’s next half-year revenue with a period that also excludes company-operated Ponsonby sales.

economy.summary: The US goods deficit widened to $149.5bn in October. Taiwan estimated third-quarter growth at 14.39% year on year. Earlier Friday releases showed faster Chinese industrial profit growth and a divergence between two Tokyo inflation measures.
economy.coverage: The full-day recap includes Friday’s official releases from Japan, China, Taiwan and the US. The Census figures were released at 21:30 Singapore time. The US spending and weekly Federal Reserve updates published after midnight belong to Saturday.
happened: US October goods imports reached $365.3bn and goods exports $215.8bn. Imports rose $21.1bn from September while exports rose $6.7bn, widening the deficit by $14.4bn.

Taiwan raised third-quarter real GDP growth to 14.39% year on year, 0.03 percentage point above its advance estimate. Real exports of goods and services grew 21.65% and gross capital formation rose 26.74%.

China’s statistics bureau reported RMB6.737tn of profits for industrial enterprises above its reporting threshold in January–October, up 16.0% year on year on a comparable basis. October alone rose 20.1%.

Preliminary Tokyo ward CPI rose 2.8% year on year in November after 2.7% in October. Excluding fresh food, inflation rose to 2.9% from 2.6%. Excluding both fresh food and energy, it eased to 2.5% from 2.6%.
key_points: The US advance estimate covers goods. Services enter the broader trade balance in a separate release.
Taiwan’s 13.28% growth for 2026 and 6.51% for 2027 are forecasts. The 14.39% third-quarter rate is a preliminary measured outcome.
The two Tokyo measures moved in opposite directions. The figures cover Tokyo’s wards and offer an early indication ahead of the national November release.
watch: Compare the advance US goods figures with the subsequent goods-and-services release and check revisions to imports.
Check the national Japanese CPI release for whether the divergence seen in Tokyo also appears across Japan.
